message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – key properties

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Common isotope** | Protium (^1H) – most abundant |
| **Other stable isotopes** | Deuterium (^2H), Tritium (^3H) – radioactive |
| **Atomic mass** | ~1.008 u (average weighted by natural abundance) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Second ionization energy** | 27.211 eV (2625 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Molecular form at STP** | Diatomic molecule (H₂) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈0.0000899 g cm⁻³) |
| **Specific heat capacity (gas, 25 °C)** | 14.304 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| **Heat of formation (gas)** | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| **Bond dissociation energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; forms hydrides with metals, acids, and many nonmetals; reacts with oxygen to form water (combustion). |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; explosive mixture with air (4–75 % H₂ in air). |
| **Uses** | Fuel cell technology, ammonia synthesis (Haber process), petroleum refining, metal processing, laboratory reagent, space propulsion. |
| **Physical state at room temperature** | Gas |
| **Color / odor / taste** | Colorless, odorless, tasteless |
| **Solubility in water** | Low (~1.6 g L⁻¹ at 20 °C) |
| **Isotopic variations** | Deuterium used in nuclear fusion research; tritium used in nuclear weapons and fusion experiments. |

These values are standard at 298 K (25 °C) and 1 atm unless otherwise noted.
